c.tagline: Pink-stone Baroque cathedrals and silver-mine history stacked up a high-desert ravine.

taxi.fareNote: Zacatecas taxis are generally not metered - agree the fare before setting off. Uber and DiDi both operate and give an up-front price, though the compact center is easiest on foot.

emergency.note: 911 is Mexico's unified emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; 078 is the national tourist assistance line.

hood_landmark.Alameda Garcia de la Cadena: Alameda Trinidad Garcia de la Cadena, Zacatecas

avoid.reason: Stay within the compact historic centre and avoid peripheral colonias and, above all, intercity highways after dark, as Zacatecas state sees serious cartel-related violence.
Petty theft can occur in markets and bus stations, so keep valuables discreet and use registered taxis at night.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed colonial heart, a warren of pink-cantera-stone streets and callejones around the Baroque cathedral, Plaza de Armas and Hidalgo Avenue; where most museums, restaurants and the nightly callejoneada street parties are, and the best base for first-timers.
A calmer, walkable pocket just west of the cathedral around the leafy Alameda park and Garcia de la Cadena, with cafes and mid-range hotels a few minutes' stroll from the main sights.

An upscale, quieter district along the old El Cubo aqueduct and the Sierra de Alica gardens, home to the landmark Quinta Real hotel built inside a 19th-century bullring; good for a refined, restful stay near the center.

The neighboring colonial town 7 km east, known for the magnificent Convento de Guadalupe and its museum of viceregal art, plus modern shopping malls and business hotels; a calmer, more spread-out place to sleep.

The steep slopes and summit of Cerro de la Bufa above town, reached by the El Teleferico cable car, with panoramic viewpoints, the Toma de Zacatecas museum, the El Eden mine and dramatic vistas; a scenic, sight-heavy edge of the city.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water only.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 06:00-22:00; the Teleferico operates about 10:00-18:00 daily, weather permitting (it stops in high winds).
transit.note: Zacatecas has no metro or light rail; the compact UNESCO center is best explored on foot, with city buses and taxis or ride apps for longer trips and the Teleferico linking the two hilltops for the views.
transit.pay: City bus fares (~MXN 9-10) are paid in cash to the driver; there is no rechargeable transit card. The Teleferico aerial tram is a tourist attraction with its own ticket, bought at the Cerro del Grillo or Cerro de la Bufa stations.
